replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

discarded_claims.claim: One open question the reviewer should settle, and it is a driver-favourable one: the pickup carries TWO registered pickup points at a TRANSPORT_HUB interchange (trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2), and no admissible chat record shows the rider naming a specific entrance, block or bay. On those facts POL-NS-03(ii), not POL-NS-03(i), is the limb that would apply if the parties simply held different faces of the same interchange — the mislocation would be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver would receive the platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. I do not ask the tribunal to find the driver was outside the arrival radius — no trace exists to show it either way — only that the reviewer resolve the pin question on the escalated record.
discarded_claims.reason: Cites EV-CHAT-00213, an artifact whose weight_multiplier is 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, without disclosing the impairment or naming the issue code as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. It refers only to 'no admissible chat record' and never states that the artifact is impaired or which issue codes fired, so the claim is discarded on the same footing as an uncited claim.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this charge cannot be settled on the automated record and goes to a human reviewer. Two independent things put it there.

1. Repeat pattern. Both profiles record 2 no-show disputes between this rider (RDR-07690) and this driver (DRV-04355) in the trailing 90 days — rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory at 2 or more, and POL-GEN-01 names exactly these two fields as citable for that test. That fact is recorded independently in both snapshots, each at full weight (1.0), and it is the ground I rest the ruling on.

2. The deciding evidence is not here. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the message export (EV-CHAT-00213) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-NS-01 requires the trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence (limb b) and to show a continuous in-geofence dwell of 300 s at this TRANSPORT_HUB bay (limb c). With no trace those limbs cannot be run at all: they are undecided, not failed. An absent instrument is the limiting case of an impaired one, and an undecided limb supports neither the fee nor a refund.

What that means for each side's arguments. The rider's refund routes do not succeed. POL-NS-02 refunds only where the trace 'contains no qualifying in-radius fix'; a trace that does not exist cannot be found to contain nothing, so it is undecided rather than failed, and no full refund can issue on it. POL-NS-04 cannot run either, because limb (a) needs the chat log to show the content of the messages, and the export is gone — the surviving trip_record's chat_message_count of 3 and empty in_app_calls show a chat existed and that no voice call was placed, but not what was said or whether it was answered. Your account that the messages went unanswered is noted, but it stands in for the missing test rather than replacing it. The driver's arguments fail the same way. POL-NS-01(d) is satisfied on the trip_record's face (terminated by the driver with RIDER_UNREACHABLE, no boarding), but limb (b) and limb (c) remain undecided, so the fee is not confirmed. The trip_record's own stamps (arrived 17:47:05, cancelled 17:53:40, wait_time_min 6.6) cannot carry the dwell for POL-NS-01(c), because that clause deliberately clocks from GPS fixes and not from the 'arrived' tap or the platform's wait counter; and POL-NS-06 cannot find a shortfall (or its absence) without a trace, with the traffic advisory also MISSING (EV-ADVIS-00213-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) so limb (i) accumulation is unavailable.

On the surviving record I did confirm two things. The $6.00 fee reconciles correctly as the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so there is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d). And the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip — 3 no-show terminations against 107 completed trips in 30 days is 2.8%, below both the count of 4 and the 8% rate — so no farming escalation and no false-arrival referral arises. No clause in this category produces a referral on these facts.

Because escalation is terminal, no money moves: the $6.00 is neither collected nor refunded but held (the ledger already shows payment_status PENDING, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), pending review. On confidence: it is not zero. The escalation is carried by the repeat-dispute pattern, recorded independently at full weight in both profiles; the missing instruments are why the merits cannot be decided, not why the escalation itself is uncertain.

Open questions for the reviewer: (i) whether the driver was in fact inside the Jurong East PHV bay for the required 300-second dwell, and whether the rider's three messages were answered — both turn on records the platform can no longer produce; and (ii) the pin question: the pickup carries two registered pickup points at this interchange, so if the parties simply held different faces of the same venue the wrong-entrance analysis in POL-NS-03 (and its pin-ambiguity treatment) may bear on the outcome.
